title: Purity of fibres under a finite dominant integral cover
statement: Let S be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme; pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let C and D be integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme] of finite type over S [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let r:D\to C be a finite dominant S-morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism; def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Assume that there is an integer n\geq0 such that every nonempty scheme-theoretic fibre C_s [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is pure of dimension n, meaning that every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of C_s has topological Krull dimension n [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then every nonempty fibre D_s is pure of dimension n.

source.place: Dimension-of-fibres discussion using openness of the bounded-dimension locus (02FZ), together with Algebra Tags 00OK and 00OY for finite integral dimension preservation; the proof adds the standard going-up argument that a component of a fibre of a finite dominant integral map maps onto a component downstairs.

proof.text: Write $f:D\to S$ and $h:C\to S$ for the structure morphisms. Finiteness makes $r$ closed, and dominance means that its image is dense; hence $r(D)=C$. For each $s\in S$, the map $r_s:D_s\to C_s$ is the base change of $r$ along $C_s\to C$, so it is finite and surjective. The two fibres are of finite type over $\kappa(s)$ by finite-type base change, and are Noetherian by finite type over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. In particular $D_s$ is nonempty exactly when $C_s$ is nonempty.

Let $\xi_D$ and $\xi_C$ be the generic points of the integral schemes $D$ and $C$. Continuity gives $r(D)\subseteq\overline{\{r(\xi_D)\}}$; Step 1 and uniqueness of generic points give $r(\xi_D)=\xi_C$. Put $t=f(\xi_D)=h(\xi_C)$, without assuming that $t$ is generic in $S$. The fibre projection identifies $|D_t|$ with the subspace $f^{-1}(t)$, which contains $\xi_D$. Any nonempty open of this subspace is $V\cap f^{-1}(t)$ for a nonempty open $V$ of $D$; it contains $\xi_D$ since every nonempty open of $D$ does. Thus $D_t$ has the point corresponding to $\xi_D$ as a dense generic point and is irreducible. The identical subspace argument with $C,h,\xi_C$ proves that $C_t$ is nonempty and irreducible.

source.place: Tags 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober) and 01K1 (lemma-fibre-topological); elementary subspace argument using the generic points of the total spaces.

proof.text: The nonempty irreducible fibre $C_t$ has itself as its unique irreducible component, so the hypothesis gives $\dim C_t=n$. Apply finite-surjective dimension preservation to $r_t$ using Step 1 to get $\dim D_t=n$. Since $D_t$ is irreducible and of finite type over $\kappa(t)$, the local dimension theorem for irreducible locally algebraic schemes gives $\dim_{\widetilde\xi_D}D_t=\dim D_t=n$. Here $\widetilde\xi_D$ is the fibre point corresponding to $\xi_D$.

For $x\in D$ let $d(x)=\dim_{\widetilde x}D_{f(x)}$, the local topological dimension in its fibre. If $n>0$, the bounded-dimension locus $U_{n-1}=\{x:d(x)\leq n-1\}$ is open in $D$ by the local-fibre-dimension openness theorem, since $f$ is locally of finite type. Step 3 says that it does not contain $\xi_D$. Every nonempty open of $D$ contains $\xi_D$, so $U_{n-1}=\varnothing$. Consequently $d(x)\geq n$ for every $x\in D$. If $n=0$, the same inequality follows directly because the local dimension at a point is nonnegative.

source.place: Tag 02FZ (lemma-openness-bounded-dimension-fibres); topology.tex Tag 0055 (definition-Krull), item (4), for n=0. The open locus is upstairs in D.

proof.text: Fix any $s$ with $D_s\ne\varnothing$. By Step 1, $C_s\ne\varnothing$, and its components all have dimension $n$ by hypothesis. Apply the equidimensional-open local-dimension theorem with $Y=O=C_s$ to get $\dim_z C_s=n$ for every $z\in C_s$. The supremum-of-local-dimensions formula then gives $\dim C_s=n$. Applying finite-surjective dimension preservation to $r_s$ yields $\dim D_s=n$. For every $x\in D_s$, the whole fibre is an open neighbourhood of $x$, so the definition of local dimension gives $\dim_xD_s\leq\dim D_s=n$.

source.place: Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), parts (3), (5); topology.tex Tag 0B7I (lemma-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions); Algebra Tags 00OK and 00OY.

proof.text: Steps 4 and 5 give $\dim_xD_s=n$ for every point of each nonempty fibre $D_s$. Step 1 makes $D_s$ locally Noetherian. Apply the constant-local-dimension component theorem to $Y=O=D_s$: every irreducible component of $D_s$ has dimension $n$. This is precisely the required purity. Fibres which are empty impose no assertion.

source.place: Tag 0055 (definition-Krull); constant local dimension and irreducible components, as stated in lem-sbc-constant-local-dimension-components.
